title: Ordinary localized projection pullback and resolving complexes
statement: For schemes X,Y of universe u, f:X to Y, coefficient ring sheaves RY,RX of universe u+1, a coefficient inverse-image isomorphism c, a normalized Global datum g, and V in Y.ProEt, there exists an exact localized Operation o with coefficient at T to V equal to the original coefficient at T.left. There exists an OrdinaryTensor mu for o satisfying its pure-unit normalization; termwise pullback by o preserves flat-term K-flat complexes. All notions are those of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction-data]. No derived tensor models, tensor shifts, derived adjunction normalizations, or restriction comparisons are asserted.

proof.text: Localize this presentation without changing site universes. Restriction of set sheaves is left adjoint to precomposition with Over.star. The product comparison identifies Over.star V followed by Over.post U with U followed by Over.star (U V). Uniqueness of composite left adjoints gives the localization isomorphism. Its unit equation follows from the two composite units, prodComparison_snd, and naturality of the global unit. Restrict the coefficient map sectionwise and conjugate the global presentation by this isomorphism.

proof.text: Construct the actual module pullback from its existing right-adjoint existence theorem. The localized ring presentation identifies its underlying abelian sheaf with abelian inverse image, compatibly with units. Forgetting further to sets gives the module presentation. Underlying abelian inverse image is left exact and module forgetful reflects finite limits. Pushforward is additive sectionwise; adjunction gives additive pullback and finite-colimit preservation. The proved containing-universe Grothendieck theorem and the source-library K-injective theorem supply K-injective resolutions. These data form Operation with the unchanged restricted coefficient.

proof.text: Use algebraic_pullback_of_presentations to lift the specified set inverse image to the actual module pullback. Apply the already proved inverse_tensor_source_unit helper of the signed-line tensor theorem. Its binary monoidal comparison and source-unit pure-tensor equation are definitionally the iso and pure_unit fields of Operation.OrdinaryTensor.

proof.text: Apply isKFlat_ringedToposPullback to this algebraic inverse image with identity scalar extension. Remove the identity scalar-extension model using systemScalarModelUnit. Transport K-flatness along the resulting complex isomorphism, and transport flatness degreewise along its evaluation isomorphisms. This gives exactly resolving preservation for arbitrary unbounded complexes.

lean.statement:
theorem localOrdinaryResolving_exists {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (R_Y : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (R_X : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (c : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R_Y ≅ R_X)
    (g : Global f R_Y R_X c) (V : Y.ProEt) :
    ∃ o : Operation (Over.post (X := V) (proEtaleBaseChange f)) (R_Y.over V)
        (R_X.over ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V)),
      (∀ T : Over V, o.coefficient.hom.app (op T) =
        g.operation.coefficient.hom.app (op T.left)) ∧
      ∃ mu : o.OrdinaryTensor,
        ∀ P, resolving (R_Y.over V) P →
          resolving (R_X.over ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V))
            ((o.pullback.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)
